summary: For the frozen obligation c1, the same CBOR NaN input satisfies the old harness assertion before g0001 and fails it after g0001.

coverage_evidence.dependency_reason: The supplied build rule compiles this CBOR fuzz target against the header.

claims.necessity_reason: The target already asserts equality after decoding, encoding, and decoding supported CBOR input; that assertion must hold for the target to run successfully.

before.requirement: For CBOR bytes {0xf9, 0x7c, 0x01}, the existing decode–encode–decode equality assertion must hold.
before.reason: The half precision value decodes to NaN, but the old floating point constructor converts it to JSON null. CBOR encoding and decoding preserve null, and two JSON null values compare equal.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The CBOR half precision branch produces NaN for the supplied bytes.
Floating point conversion calls the external constructor.
The CBOR serializer encodes JSON null as 0xf6.
The CBOR decoder restores 0xf6 as JSON null.
The JSON equality operator considers two null values equal.

after.requirement: For the same CBOR bytes {0xf9, 0x7c, 0x01}, the existing decode–encode–decode equality assertion must hold.
after.reason: The changed constructor retains NaN as a JSON float. CBOR encoding writes a double precision float, decoding restores NaN, and the existing equality operator compares the two NaNs with ordinary floating point ==, which is false.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The same CBOR half precision input produces NaN after the change.
Floating point conversion calls the external constructor.
The CBOR serializer writes the retained float as a double precision value.
The second CBOR decode restores the double precision NaN.
JSON float equality uses ordinary floating point ==.

claims.comparison_reason: The same input and unchanged harness reach the assertion on both sides. Before g0001, NaN becomes null and the assertion passes. After g0001, NaN remains a float and the assertion fails.
